I'm not sure whether it is worth doing so, may you give some advice?

I think there was a consensus that CNI plugins are not supposed to return an error in this case?
@dcbw @squeed

This is a bug, probably in the container runtime. Kubernetes + docker implements the correct behavior, which is to pass the empty string when the container no longer exists.

The CNI spec, as usual, is somewhat ambiguous:

>   - When `CNI_NETNS` and/or `prevResult` are not provided, the plugin should clean up as many resources as possible (e.g. releasing IPAM allocations) and return a successful response.

We've clearly interpreted "not provided" to mean "empty string".

Looking at the filed bug (#84147), I see that the code is complaining about a bad path to `/proc/<PID>/ns/net`, which is very, VERY wrong. In the event of pid reuse, you will find yourself tearing down the network of another process. **The eth0 you tear down could be your uplink!**
Actually I would like to let CRI deletion interface return an idempotent result. That would be better.

> which is to pass the empty string when the container no longer exists

what if the network has been torn down, but the container failed to get destroyed. And kubelet will retry to remove the container, ....

issue_context.title: cni "no such file or directory" error check may cause a false positive
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

For some cni plugins that rely on additional necessary resources(e.g. grpc unix socket), if the resource is not found, the plugin would return an error that is similar to `connect: no such file or directory`. On this occasion, kubelet would consider this as a duplicate deletion of network resource that has already been deleted in previous attempts and report no error.

**What you expected to happen**:

kubelet should check `no such file or directory` failure more precisely to distinguish cni plugin error message.
Otherwise, cni plugins will have to replace `no such file or directory` error message in some other synonymous  words.

review_comments:
If possible I would prefer checking the error code for the "well-known" error codes see: https://github.com/containernetworking/cni/blob/master/pkg/types/types.go#L139 + https://github.com/containernetworking/cni/blob/master/SPEC.md#well-known-error-codes instead of parsing the strings (which will probably not that performant).

Also I think this should be moved to a common place rather than be duplicated in code e.g. somewhere here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/dockershim/network/plugins.go
Hm it seems like these codes are not available in this method :(
I don't think the message checking code here is right. Either `no such file or directory` or `failed to Statfs` should be considered as network disabled or missing.
And I'd prefer to make `noSuchNetNS` as a common util function.
Both the `no such file or directory` and `failed to Statfs` cannot ensure the NetNS does not exist if the cni plugin does not invoke the oommonly-used function `ns.GetNS()`
